samples.summary: Backend re-implements the shared band walk instead of calling `bandBlockNumerics`, and the two copies already disagree
samples.evidence: This change introduces `bandBlockNumerics(blocks)` in `@wafflebase/docs` (`packages/docs/src/model/numeric-attrs.ts:293`) as the single walk that bands a codec-free docs block list — lineHeight, listLevel, inline fontSize, inline image size, rowHeights, columnWidths, cell padding, colSpan/rowSpan — and every other new reader calls it (`yorkie-slides-store.ts`, `yorkie-board-store.ts`, `packages/slides/src/model/band-numerics.ts`). The v1 slides `PUT` arm instead hand-rolls the same walk in `bandSlideBlockNumerics` / `bandSlideCellNumerics` plus the fontSize branch bolted into `normalizeSlideInlines`, in a file that already imports from `@wafflebase/docs` (the diff adds `normalizeCellPadding`, `normalizeColumnRatio`, `normalizeFontSize`, … to that import). The duplicate is already divergent: the controller bands `style.fontSize` on an inline but never `style.image.width/height`, while `bandBlockNumerics` drops an out-of-band image pair via `isPaintableImageSize`. So a `PUT` carrying `image: {width: 1e9, height: 1e9}` is accepted, echoed and stored, and every reader (`YorkieSlidesStore.read()`, the board store, the revision preview) then silently drops it — two answers to the same question, and exactly the write-side/read-side divergence the bands are documented to close (`docs/design/docs/docs.md`: "the v1 `PUT` bands on write … and the collaborative path bands on read" using "the same normalizers").

samples.summary: `YorkieSlidesStore` keeps a private `bandElementText` walk instead of the new shared `bandElementNumerics` it motivated
samples.evidence: The change adds `packages/slides/src/model/band-numerics.ts` whose header states the walk exists so that "a fourth reader is a call rather than a fourth chance to forget", and `docs/design/docs/docs.md` records the same: "the walk lives in one place — `bandSlidesDocumentNumerics` / `bandElementNumerics` / `bandLayoutNumerics` … and each reader calls it". The board store (`yorkie-board-store.ts:442`) and the snapshot adapters do call it; the slides store — the reader the design section is written about — instead defines a private `bandElementText(type, data)` covering the shape and table branches by hand, and only imports `bandLayoutNumerics`. Two implementations of the same rule that the doc claims is singular, free to drift (the shared one also has the 32-deep group cap and the `text` branch).

samples.summary: `PUT /content` validation contract in rest-api.md not updated for the new numeric repair, and its losslessness claim is now false
samples.evidence: rest-api.md §5.5 is the canonical spec of the `PUT` contract and this change alters it without touching the doc: the endpoint now silently *repairs* present-but-wrong numerics on slides bodies (clamping `fontSize`/`lineHeight`/`listLevel`/spans/column ratios, dropping non-finite ones), whereas the doc scopes repair to *absent* values and says "A value that is present but wrong is still a 400" and "the values inside a repaired collection … are stored as given". The doc also asserts "`GET` → edit → `PUT` stays lossless for docs bodies: the read side of the Tree codec drops exactly the values the validator rejects" — the diff's own comment in `packages/docs/src/model/crdt-attrs.ts` now states the opposite for `lineHeight` (`PUT` accepts `1e9`, the reader clamps it to `MAX_LINE_HEIGHT`; `0`/`-2` are accepted and read as absent). Design-doc discipline: the behavioural contract moved, the canonical doc did not.
searchedFor: diff hunks for docs/design/* (only docs.md, docs-pagination.md, tables/docs-table-row-splitting.md touched)

samples.summary: The change widens the pre-existing duplicate Tree parser rather than reusing the engine's reader
samples.evidence: `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts` is, by the change's own test comment, "a *duplicate* parser of `packages/docs/src/model/crdt-tree.ts`". This diff adds eight more band call sites (`normalizeFontSize`, `isPaintableImageSize`, `normalizeCellPadding`, `normalizeTableSpan`, `parseColumnWidthsAttr`, `normalizeRowHeight`, `normalizeListLevel`, `sanitizeDocStyles`) to the copy, each of which must now be kept in lockstep with the engine copy by hand. The constants/normalizers are shared (good), but the walk is not; the change extends a divergence surface it was well placed to collapse, and the only thing keeping the two honest is two separate test suites.

samples.summary: Change bundles two unrelated efforts: the #1050 list-subtree gesture and a cross-package numeric-hardening program
samples.evidence: Roughly half the diff implements issue #1050 (subtree-carrying indent/outdent: `list-level.ts` planner, `Doc.siblingBlocksOf`, batching/undo and caret-flush rework in `editor.ts`, `text-editor.ts`, `text-box-editor.ts`), and the other half is an independent hardening program spanning backend v1 `PUT`, both CRDT parsers, the paste sanitizer, the DOCX importer, the named-style registry, the paginator's `MAX_ROW_PAGE_SPAN`, `computeTableLayout` step 5d, slides/board stores and revision-preview adapters. Only `normalizeListLevel` genuinely links them. No originating issue text was supplied for the second half, so I cannot confirm it was asked for; if it was not, this is scope past #1050 that makes the change hard to review or revert as a unit.

The new `walkCellsForSiblings` is a copy of the existing `walkCellsForBlock` recursion differing only in what it returns (the containing `cell.blocks` rather than the block), and `siblingBlocksOf` likewise mirrors `findBlock`'s region/parent-map/full-walk shape. One parameterised walk (or returning the container alongside the block) would keep the two resolution orders from drifting.

verdict.reason: The finding is accurate as described. `bandBlockNumerics` is the shared, exported band walk (packages/docs/src/model/numeric-attrs.ts:293, exported at index.ts:112 / node.ts:155) and is the single copy every other reader uses (slides/src/model/band-numerics.ts:51,57,68,115; yorkie-slides-store.ts:66,436,509,517,536; yorkie-board-store.ts:39,383,1333,1368). The v1 slides PUT arm instead re-implements it: `bandSlideBlockNumerics` (docs-content.controller.ts:1027) and `bandSlideCellNumerics` (:1060) mirror `bandOneBlock` field-for-field and even comment-for-comment (controller:1049-1055 vs numeric-attrs:343-348; controller:1070-1072 vs numeric-attrs:365-367), plus a fontSize branch bolted into `normalizeSlideInlines` (:1203-1208). Reuse was available and cheap: the same file already imports seven normalizers plus MAX_TABLE_COLUMNS from '@wafflebase/docs' (:44-57) and the package is a declared dependency (packages/backend/package.json:46). The copies have already diverged: `bandOneBlock` drops an out-of-band inline `style.image` pair via `isPaintableImageSize` (numeric-attrs.ts:323-332), while a case-insensitive grep for `image` across the entire controller yields only two comment hits (:749, :1148) — the PUT path never bands inline image size, so `image:{width:1e9,height:1e9}` is echoed and stored on write and silently dropped by every reader. No guard elsewhere covers this. The design doc explicitly frames write-side and read-side as applying "the same normalizers" and states the walk should live in one place (docs/design/docs/docs.md:262-289). Under this lens, duplicated logic that has already diverged and gives two answers to the same question is major.
